body:
An Easter reflection—and what our investigations uncovered about Colorado this week
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
---
**April 5, 2026** **SUNDAY NEWS DIGEST**
| | Dear Rocky Mountain Voice family,
**Today is Easter.**
And before we get into the headlines, it’s worth slowing down for just a moment. This week's [Easter devotional by Pastor Drake Hunter](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) reminds us that what we’re seeing play out in culture right now—division, public shaming, the instinct to tear people down—isn’t new. It’s human.
Long before social media, there was a crowd. Long before cancellation, there was a cross. But Easter tells a different story.
It’s the story of a God who doesn’t cancel people—He cancels what stands against them. A God who chose restoration over rejection. And in a time when it feels like everything is about tearing down, that truth matters more than ever.
Because if we’re honest... the same instincts we see in the world today aren’t just “out there.” They’re in all of us. Easter is the reminder that there’s a better way. ✝️
\--
**Now, onto our most shocking RMV original investigations this week:** Elections—and trust—took center stage again. A Denver judge ordered the Secretary of State’s office to [reopen a campaign finance case out of Pueblo](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) after finding the state didn’t fully investigate key evidence. The ruling didn’t declare wrongdoing—but it did say the process fell short.
At the same time, a [former top aide to Secretary of State Jena Griswold is now speaking out publicly](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), describing what he says was a culture of retaliation, blurred lines between politics and public duty, and even the use of encrypted messaging to limit transparency.
Layer onto that a [new federal election order](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) that could fundamentally reshape Colorado’s mail ballot system—forcing new voter verification processes and raising serious questions about how same-day registration would work moving forward.
And then there’s the Tina Peters case—where [convictions were upheld, but her sentence was thrown out](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) and sent back for reconsideration, reopening one of the most high-profile election cases in the state.
Meanwhile, what’s being presented as “grassroots”... may not be so simple. The “No Kings” protests drew large crowds across Colorado this week. But behind the messaging of decentralized activism, records show a [coordinated national operation](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)—complete with centralized training, funding networks, and structured messaging distributed to organizers.
And then there’s the promise vs. reality story Coloradans are paying attention to. When marijuana was legalized, voters were told schools would benefit. More than a decade later, Colorado has collected over $3.1 billion in marijuana tax revenue. But [only a fraction of that has made its way into classrooms](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)—and an even smaller portion into actual day-to-day school funding.
The bigger picture... Transparency. Accountability. And whether the systems we rely on are still working the way people believe they are. And maybe that’s why the Easter message matters so much right now. Because truth without grace becomes harsh. And grace without truth becomes hollow.
In truth & liberty, Team RMV
---
| | |
---
| | **TOP STORIES OF THE WEEK**
---
**[Colorado collected $3.1 billion in marijuana taxes. Here’s how much actually reaches schools.](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) When Colorado voters said yes to legal marijuana back in 2012, schools were a big part of the pitch. More than a decade in, the state has collected over 3.1 billion dollars in tax revenue. So where does it all go?

**[“Single most insecure person I’ve ever encountered”: Former Griswold aide breaks silence ahead of AG race](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY JEN SCHUMANN, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) Reese Edwards didn’t plan to speak out. He spent less than a year inside Colorado’s Secretary of State’s office before leaving in 2020, frustrated and burned out enough to walk away. He wasn’t looking to revisit any of it. Now, with Jena Griswold running for attorney general, he’s speaking up—and doing it on the record.
**[The numbers didn’t add up: A judge says Colorado’s elections office didn’t either](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY JEN SCHUMANN, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) Jonathan Ambler read the article more than once. Republicans in Pueblo County had reported tens of thousands in contributions. Democrats—who had controlled local politics for generations and operated out of their own headquarters—had reported barely a few thousand.

|
---
**LEGISLATIVE SESSION**
_**Quick Summary of the Week:**_ 🏛️ _**In the Senate:** Senate Republicans highlighted a key legislative win this week with the signing of _[SB-011](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)_ , a bill requiring social media companies to comply with warrants like any other entity—aimed at helping law enforcement respond more quickly to crimes involving online platforms. At the same time, lawmakers raised concerns over new Democrat-backed proposals, including _[SB-008](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)_ , which critics say would bypass TABOR by creating a new fee-funded enterprise tied to internet services, potentially increasing costs for Coloradans. Meanwhile, senators also recognized Denim Day at the Capitol, honoring survivors and raising awareness about sexual assault._
🏛️ _**In the House:** House Republicans focused heavily on parental rights this week, opposing bills they say shift decision-making away from families and toward government—particularly _[SB26-018](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)_ , which would limit public access to minors’ name-change records and sparked debate over whether parental consent should be required. While several bipartisan bills advanced through the chamber on issues ranging from public safety to professional licensing, Republicans also highlighted ongoing concerns about the state budget, noting Colorado is facing a $1.5 billion deficit and a structural shortfall that could continue without major reforms._

|
---
**[Attorneys raise concerns over certification tied to Colorado court system access](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) Colorado attorneys are starting to push back after a certification prompt began appearing when they log into the state’s court e-filing system. The requirement traces back to Senate Bill 25-276 and related statutes, including C.R.S. § 24-74-105, which deal with how the state handles nonpublic personal identifying information.
**[When “Protecting Seniors” Meets Fiscal Reality: A Self-Inflicted Crisis](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY REP. KEN DEGRAAF, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) _Any legislator who has opened their inbox lately has seen the urgent appeals: AARP warning that Colorado’s Senior Homestead Property Tax Exemption is under threat. The message is emotionally compelling—and fundamentally correct._
__
**[Colorado Progressives Blame TABOR For $1.5B Budget Gap While Expanding Costly Tax Credits](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** [COMPLETE COLORADO](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) _Karl Marx, co-author of The Communist Manifesto, once wrote “History repeats itself, first as tragedy, then as farce.” We’re watching a version of this play out at the Colorado State Capitol._ __
__**[READ MORE ON LEGISLATIVE SESSION](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** __

|
---
**STATE**
**[Federal order puts Colorado’s mail ballot system on a collision course](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY JEN SCHUMANN, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) The way Colorado runs elections hasn’t changed—but a new federal order could force it to. The order would have federal agencies assemble a nationwide list of verified U.S. citizens and share it with state election officials.

**[Tina Peters convictions upheld, sentence thrown out and case sent back to Mesa County court](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY JEN SCHUMANN, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) Tina Peters remains convicted—but the case that made her a national figure isn’t over. A Colorado appeals court upheld every conviction against the former Mesa County clerk Thursday, while also throwing out her sentence and ordering resentencing after finding the trial judge improperly weighed her speech about election fraud.
**[Grassroots or guided? Inside the ‘No Kings’ protests in Colorado](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) A large crowd gathered at the Colorado State Capitol last Saturday before marching through downtown Denver — the third installment of a movement its organizers describe on their national website as a grassroots uprising, “spreading from small towns to city centers and across every community determined to defend democracy.” Denver was one of many across the state.

_**[READ MORE STATE NEWS](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**_
|
---
**NATIONAL**
**[The Plain Truth Behind Voter ID, the SAVE America Act and Election Integrity](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY RUSS MINARY, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) _Congress has been dithering on a number of issues that impact legal, law-abiding US citizens and taxpayers. House and Senate reps from both parties are dragging their feet for various reasons._
**[Critics Question Why States Share Voter Data With Leftist Groups But Not DHS](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**[THE FEDERALIST](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) _Democrat senators claim it is an unconstitutional invasion of privacy that the SAVE America Act requires states to share voter rolls and requisite identifying information with the federal government in order to check for noncitizens, but many of their states already share the same data with left-wing third party organizations._
__
**[Vance Announces White House Review Of Omar Immigration Claims](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**[THE DAILY SIGNAL](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) Vice President JD Vance alleges that Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., committed immigration fraud. “Ilhan Omar definitely committed immigration fraud against the United States of America,” he said when asked if Omar committed fraud by conservative activist and podcast host Benny Johnson on “The Benny Johnson Show.”
_**[READ MORE NATIONAL NEWS](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**_
|
---
**LOCAL**
**[Denver in Decline](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY TOM ANTHONY, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) _My great grandpa excavated Federal Blvd and Colfax with mules and a scraper, his dad having been on the third wagon train into Denver in 1858. For many years I owned and developed Denver property out of the commitment: “Sustainable Cities People Love,” my company motto._

**[20 Years Probation For Sexual Assault On a Child](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**[JEFFCO KIDS FIRST](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) _I was in the Jefferson County Courthouse earlier this afternoon, and the world doesn’t make sense anymore. I watched a school social worker admit to sexual assault of a student and get sentenced to probation with zero prison time._

**[Former Colorado Teacher Of The Year Finalist Sentenced To 14 Years In Student Abuse Case](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**[CBS COLORADO](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) A finalist for 2025 Colorado Teacher of the Year violated the terms of her probation and continued to contact one of her former students after she’d been criminally charged for having a relationship with the student and fired from her teaching position, according to a court document.

**_[READ MORE LOCAL NEWS](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)_**
|
---
**COMMENTARY**
**[Self-Governance Is Not a Spectator Sport](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** REP. KEN DEGRAAF, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) _Here is the truth: if citizens want constitutional, accountable representation in Colorado, they must invest in it. We are rightly proud of the principle that helped found this Republic—no taxation without representation. But in today’s political reality, there is a necessary corollary: there is no meaningful representation without participation._ __
**[Denver’s growth dilemma: More housing, less breathing room](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY NEIL WOLKODOFF, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) _In the past, residents enjoyed Denver for a positive lifestyle and outdoor recreational activities. That was the past; is the push to control housing changing that for the worse? Regrettably, the answer is yes._ __
**[Speak up or step back: Why critics say Coloradans must engage with CPW now](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**[COLORADO ACCOUNTABILITY PROJECT](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) _Depending on where you get your news, you are probably by now aware that the CPW Commissioners, in a meeting that I’ve heard referred to as a “shit-show” by more than one person, voted to accept a petition by a monied, out of state group. If you missed it or want to hit the high spots again, I put a FencePost article on the meeting. That is the first link below._
__
**_[READ MORE COMMENTARY](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)_**

For Christians, it reflects the empty tomb—its hard shell symbolizing the sealed grave, and the breaking of it representing the Resurrection. The White House Easter Egg Roll dates back to 1878.

Peter – there are TONS of terrible GOP candidates running in 2026. And, of course, Donald Trump has endorsed LOTS of them.
Here are some of the WORST of the WORST:
**🔴 TOMMY TUBERVILLE – Alabama – Governor**
In 2023, Tommy Tuberville held up hundreds of military promotions for nearly a year – a move that drew bipartisan condemnation and left 89% of all general officer positions in the U.S. military affected by his actions. On top of that, Tuberville violated the STOCK Act – which prohibits members of Congress from trading on insider information – 132 times in a single year.
**🔴 VIVEK RAMASWAMY – Ohio – Governor**
Vivek Ramaswamy is an out-of-touch billionaire who has said Medicare and Medicaid were “mistakes.” During his 2024 presidential campaign, he proposed ENDING birthright citizenship. And now Trump wants to put him in the governor's mansion in Ohio – a state where working families can't afford more MAGA experiments.
**🔴 JOHN SUNUNU – New Hampshire – U.S. Senate**
John Sununu spent nearly two decades working as a lobbyist for Big Oil, Big Pharma, and Wall Street – collecting millions from giant corporate interests. His 2002 Senate victory was tainted by a Republican phone-jamming scandal that deliberately suppressed Democratic voter turnout on Election Day. And now he's back, having reversed course on a president he publicly called "a loser" the moment it became politically convenient.
**🔴 MICHAEL WHATLEY – North Carolina – U.S. Senate**
Michael Whatley isn't just endorsed by Donald Trump – he was personally recruited by him. As RNC Chairman, he spread false claims about Democratic cities engaging in “massive fraud.” He spent years as a lobbyist for Big Oil companies. And now he’s hoping to buy North Carolina’s open U.S. Senate seat in what will be one of the most expensive + competitive races of the cycle.
**The pattern here isn't an accident. Trump is endorsing candidates in his own image – people that will rubber-stamp his agenda, no matter who gets hurt.**
We can stop it. But only with your help, Peter.

In July 1971, Henry Kissinger [boarded a flight from Islamabad](https://substack.com/redirect/fa4b5c55-3a69-4c6e-854a-7b19e4e210a4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to Beijing that supposedly didn't exist. After feigning illness, the National Security Advisor took a covert trip to China that laid the groundwork for Nixon's later visit. All of this was possible due to Pakistan's president efforts to create a secret backchannel--one that ultimately reshaped the Cold War as Kissinger managed to cleave Beijing away from Moscow. It may have been the most consequential piece of shuttle diplomacy of the 20th century...and it ran through a country that didn't exist in 1946 and that most Americans couldn't find on a map.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/ddb608eb-d2ca-486c-ba57-1e6e31a3af8c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
And now, 55 years later, Pakistan appears poised to once again play a [key role](https://substack.com/redirect/669eb925-74a6-410c-9c71-126cb68580de?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in global affairs. With the U.S. on the verge of another Forever War, a politically problematic development for the Trump Administration, the US President is eager to find an off ramp. Turns out America's "frenemy" might be the only country in the world capable of throwing Washington a lifeline.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..0HHzjlfZFQlCOkfbRCwgDCqYaPbyaYVWpOS2hnw-OaM?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=193281371)
How's that? To start, it has the only phone that rings in both Washington and Tehran. Pakistan is [the only country with direct access to both the American and Iranian leadership](https://substack.com/redirect/32c83998-154e-4c66-87ba-84f71657d8c5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Field Marshal Asim Munir, Pakistan's military chief, had [an unprecedented one-on-one lunch with Trump at the White House](https://substack.com/redirect/5565d5d7-4c5e-4a5d-a060-e924b67eaf79?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--the first time a sitting president has received Pakistan's military chief without civilian leadership present. Meanwhile, Iran's President Pezeshkian [called Pakistan's prime minister on March 28](https://substack.com/redirect/c3e2d701-0d73-4c96-8804-2289676e4add?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), praising Islamabad's "supportive role for peace."
It doesn't appear that any other nation could even make make both calls. This is especially important right now because the usual go-betweens--Oman and Qatar--are _under Iranian missile fire_.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/af0a713b-2b53-41f8-8628-16ea208f2514?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Pakistan also has plenty of motivation. It depends on the Strait of Hormuz for most of its oil imports. It also has a close relationship and [mutual defense pact with Saudi Arabia](https://substack.com/redirect/32c83998-154e-4c66-87ba-84f71657d8c5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that could drag it into the war. But perhaps most importantly for the Pakistani leadership, it faces a restive domestic population. After Israel killed Khamenei, [22 people were killed in domestic protests](https://substack.com/redirect/ef3575ac-727c-4fc4-91be-2c6c229746e2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and a mob breached the American consulate in Karachi with the goal of burning it down.
Pakistan, a predominantly Sunni country, also has the second largest Shia population in the world after Iran. Keeping the peace internally is a regular domestic objective in this traditionally fractious country. Indeed, with so many religious, ethnic, and ideological divisions, I have long felt that the country's military is the sole institution capable of preventing Pakistan's disintegration. (Incidentally, I was a member of the Board of Directors of the US Pakistan Business Council in 2007 when General Pervez Musharraf was ousted as head of the country; many of us who were watching the country closely were very worried about civilian leadership competing with the military to run the country...)
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..0HHzjlfZFQlCOkfbRCwgDCqYaPbyaYVWpOS2hnw-OaM?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=193281371)
But there are also the personal motivations of Pakistan's current Prime Minister, Shebaz Sharif. He is very eager to be seen as relevant on the global stage. After decades of pursuit for political success while languishing in his brother's shadow, he finally has risen to the top and wants to make the most of it. He is also desperate to distract from Pakistan's domestic problems, which includes a lackluster economy and the persecution of his primary political opponent, Imran Khan. Sharif has also been aggressive courting Trump; he even nominated him for the Nobel Peace Prize. Helping to end the war would place him at the center of world events...while likely also earning him Trump's recognition.
There's also the extra bonus of putting India "on its backfoot," as they say in Islamabad. [India](https://substack.com/redirect/6014d6d3-ca78-43ed-bfcb-06b1cc40b3fd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) is Pakistan's nemesis and Islamabad sees everything through the prism of potential conflict with its nuclear neighbor. It will seize any opportunity to gain an advantage. Modi visited Israel right before the strikes began, which torpedoed India's claim to neutrality and has sidelined the Hindu nation ever since. _Foreign Policy_ called it ["a humiliating failure for Modi."](https://substack.com/redirect/868361e6-8c9a-42e3-b9c1-ce54c55b1c51?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) See the video below for Pakistani interpretation of India's Israel connection.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/44434e14-f215-47fe-a78a-54d69cb8b591?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
If Pakistan actually brokers a deal, bringing it closer to the U.S., gaining prestige among Middle-Eastern countries, and making it a player on the world stage, the geopolitical implications for South Asia are enormous. It is already the only Muslim country with nukes (holder of the so-called "Islamic Bomb") and its ascent to a diplomatic powerhouse would enhance its stature.
While it's unclear if the country can broker peace, Pakistan is already seeing its status rise. On March 29, the [foreign ministers of Saudi Arabia, Egypt, and Turkey all flew to Islamabad](https://substack.com/redirect/c3e2d701-0d73-4c96-8804-2289676e4add?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). That's three of the Middle East's biggest armies, financial heft, and diplomatic clout all calling on a country that is more closely associated with instability than statesmanship. They produced a five-point peace plan calling for an immediate ceasefire and the reopening of Hormuz. Then Pakistan's foreign minister flew to Beijing, where [China endorsed the effort](https://substack.com/redirect/669eb925-74a6-410c-9c71-126cb68580de?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and issued a joint statement. Further, according to [Reuters](https://substack.com/redirect/6014d6d3-ca78-43ed-bfcb-06b1cc40b3fd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Israel removed Iran's foreign minister and parliament speaker from its assassination target list--supposedly at Pakistan's request.
* * *
## [Turnings, Upswings, and End Times](https://substack.com/redirect/bc28fd24-9cf0-43ad-9e47-ac534cc55df8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

In 1971, Pakistan was smaller, weaker and in the middle of its own crisis, fighting a civil war in what's now Bangladesh. It still somehow managed to play an outsized role in world affairs, arranging Kissinger's flight to Beijing. Today's Pakistan is similarly fragile, similarly improbable, and similarly positioned at the one intersection that matters.

As has often been said, **history may not repeat itself, but often does rhyme.**

## Missing F-15E Crew Member Rescued in Iran
U.S. forces [rescued the second crew member](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2ypCAUhJ9GMyxEfkwINjGbTTe0jnDOyBbCFDBj-fZb7r1vcNPurq7--s9jfUCIIT1_w4G2UV4TnjVia1hWCOWAVLC6N3qCUoPHTG3HVXChGZeM69VDiNcqe28JUeDUox2NUdJwbkS_W3BuFoRqkpuZYTKbk5orMspNanMz9cHebVxyPXJu1DhIMsJ7OZKbRq8ldZKjDy2X4W8Oqe1I8cofLIPLRx_t3tqrdtOvTiydWM7zHNLmborbv5Vcou_EEgqkTiwVXU6efbExYqNCdkJldc-N3Rn2DcwqEMaLvSvLRMEFiJVVuFhxCYTWep77Yv3rDDGGqk0n-fOAEP_Paj_68mPFvwAAAP__NieKGw) from an F-15E shot down over Iran, pulling the seriously wounded colonel from a mountain crevice after 36 hours behind enemy lines. The CIA [ran a deception campaign](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDtuwzAQRE9DdRT4M5kULNKoc9qUwkq7tDagRIOiLfj2gZIjpBtggBm893Udr8CZt9snrBRbKuNGx56pNaojcF1hq7TPD8IEdWekktpCo1HGS-Wk8iMC59foOoyJyJDtKOoQLi4oFUy3RDu9z3oKFr0J9i0BYaDJzmAn9DB523E815RTXisVLrp3KRhEp9NsNXqXhFOE3ErtvwtvbaGUX-VJtZ_L2uW4tHbfhf0QZhBmOI6jf8FSytkKM5w4wgxQG8-ZzvjYZSolE0qusMk_PInl2Ail1kZr77Tpl7bmrka8H5wz7z4Ip24rcP69bf9y9YzmJwAA__-j0H5L) inside Iran, spreading false reports that the airman had already been found while intelligence teams pinpointed his actual location. Hundreds of special forces and dozens of aircraft carried out the extraction, striking Iranian forces who were closing in and destroying two transport planes that got stuck before evacuating. [See the details of the mission](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO8yAQhJ8GdxthgiEpKP7GXf72SmttlnhPGCIgsfL2J9_dG1wzzUif5puP23RDjpzu_3Ej10KeEu01UmtUJuSyYSpUlyf5gKWypxzaSpOSyoDUIM3kkeN70p13gUjRuSPXWztoK6VV3erUbJeLV_180UHPs6HrhQZL12E2FDwuHbuDJrU0vZR26E86WOW97sNy7r3RQWhJnlsup8_Mqa0U4ju_qJyWvHXRra09qjj_E2oUakzvR67tqIQaD7BQo9RHDEKNey7Rw6Eo1Pis8OsGAfoBfnSBE3DBBDu3FSphhEa4gYGFEcqzEmDy4AnbCqHkDXDOLxJq7Irzj51j5Gqs0PK-Icfvke1Pz76c-goAAP__TXaMtw). President Trump then [warned Iran to reopen](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2u4yAUhJ8Gd0SAMSQFxTbusu2WFmsO4az4ieA4Ufbpr3xf4dajmdH3_blvd48Z6-O3L-Aotq3Ce2Qggr557MXXDmM_IETfBwZokRJsSijDhebCbMFj_mx6Ci4CKJgncNLaRVshrJqS0xrCvBgthVHy5n3ws_xr9G1ZjDRiERO6c01oYaQQdpEXHa0KQcu4zzIYHZkWEJBav_xrWClBzJ_2gn7ZW5myS0TPweZfTK1MrZQgYc5nxtSaWoETiKnVh4IVB3VP2CpT63KV5nq1nPpRnpxSB09QB8fuK8caux_Uj52ODvysIfEWeWq9HP-ZWqfuwvONOeMwlmnxKB6_byf6kceXU18BAAD___vwiHs) the Strait of Hormuz by Tuesday or face strikes on power plants and bridges. (Warning: strong language in link.)
## Artemis II Crew Reaches Moon Today
The Artemis II astronauts are set to [fly around the far side of the moon](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLHO4yAQhJ_G7rDWGENcUFyTLtdeaW1gifeEIQISK2__y3mFv9qVZjSab_7d1hty5PT4izvZFvKa6KiRWqOyIpcdU6HqXuQDlsqecmgbrRKkFqAE6NUjx8-qem8DkaSpJzsaMysDYGS_WSJz0XIiWhZ9N_I-X6QDULDoWdEC0LM900CBHgHMPA4qGOm9GoObRq9V6BSQ55bL8D9zahuF-MlvKoPLex_t1tqzdtOfTl47eT2OY0h3d1Kceiev1TElR-f3xO_F0mjnKpgF1lZywlerglOj8mY6xNcn9pyTCFjEiS0SVhTFJZRaz1r1xfrnwTFy1aZT8NiR47dQ-9WKbyt_AgAA__877Iea) today, becoming the first humans to travel beyond Earth orbit in more than 50 years. The four crew members will break the Apollo 13 distance record at around 1:56 p.m. ET, reaching 252,757 miles from Earth, roughly 4,100 miles farther than any human has traveled. At closest approach, they'll pass within 4,066 miles of the lunar surface and photograph parts of the far side never seen by human eyes. A solar eclipse viewed from the capsule will cap the flyby. [Watch a video here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO8yAQhJ8GuljrNYakoPgbd_nbKxFhF5s7bCLMxcrbn3yvcN1II32a-T7u7u5TTtv8369sWyxu42PP3BpX51Nd_VZ5D99M0dc9EZfYFnYIqC-gLqAd-ZTfTkmykRl5kGx7Y0ZlAAzKxaobcRiJdFDotYYrMD7MzUS-ec3XIJM9aaBA9wBm7DsVDRKpPoahJ62iUMCUWqndZ0lbWzjmd3lx7UJZZbZLa89dDP8ETgKn4zi6xyOcncDpPCNwep3DzxB4oHH-Ipy5yGrpeaSc066NUDCvPuVfZvuTiJfFnwAAAP__6w1x2w). Commander Reid Wiseman called the mission a "magnificent accomplishment." Canadian astronaut Jeremy Hansen said the view leaves the photos in the dust: "_It is another level of amazing up here."_
## Applebee's Manager Shelters 50 from Tornado
An Applebee's manager in Three Rivers, Michigan, [led 50 customers and staff](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuwyAURb_G3ogeGJt4YOiSLV07Wq_mEqiwsYAmyt9XaT-h89U9Rzof1-XKMcX99s4bbPN52fGoCa2hLBzLxntBXb_hPJcaHbJvAYsiNQnSgqbFcUzPRffOekBh6GGlMaM2REb1werzrM3ovV9HI4nmsyYGe5LjDL067qN90UjTJInMKE_aG-Wcln4dpJu07zTBxZbL6SvHvQX49Mx3lNOatz7Z0NpRu-GtU5dOXQ7kI-E1derCx5HwCVSx8c43FNFy2dllUQNSQxEjib-HCBwTnOAqAkoWUs7DNE9DX6w7HjGlWCfTabptHNOvuf0r192qnwAAAP__qLJ_Cg) to safety in the restaurant's kitchen when an EF-2 tornado struck the area last month. Aubrey McKenzie, who has been [afraid of storms since childhood](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD0SmzAQhU8DnTySkMEUKtLQOW1KZpFWsBn9MCvZjm-fIVdI_X7mve_Xc30CRcr7T0hoWyhrxk-N2BryCsQJMmN1L_QBuJLHEtqBq5Z6FNIIOa4eKH5X03sbEDUOPVo1TXczSTnp_rAzImx35eZhxsfm1QDOaPWYh4cKcDfQk73apJGjknK6q5sJk_beqOAG5UcTOiPRUyt8-10otwND_JY38s2V1Ed7tHbWbvjR6aXTy4eiK3-uEyecyPUydXppByMKpjdyFXCeETfEKhJk2JHFARTRi1BYnFwaukZ5F66k9MrUviJh2q6kf_EltMIZfOn00rP154dipDpOnZF7Aor_hrX_ovm2-m8AAAD___LwjeE), got everyone into the kitchen in about 90 seconds as 130 mph winds shattered windows and sent debris flying from a nearby store. No one sheltered in the kitchen was injured. The tornado tore an 11-mile path through the area, injuring 10 people and severely damaging a Menards two doors down. McKenzie said she was surprised she kept it together. _"Your ears were popping. It was loud. By the sound of it, you'd think these walls weren't going to hold,"_ she recalled.

## El Paso Ranked No. 2 Best Big City
El Paso has [landed near the top](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDHO4yAQRk-Du4nwmGCnoNjGXbbd0gIzOCgTEwHrxLdfsVf46yc9fe_7c1_uNnLct9_2RaZ-Q1p2-hSmWikvxG9b0p7QxW2N9cw27nHfnF1QogapQOrF28jnojpvnPS3viPTj-NVjQPehu5h5OSdtqsbxsmvkxpG54N2NPYYvHN-6qJpMqmk7nvZ4-3iPalBruE6OAqOtFCSfKwpX-qDKn1tCXymg_JlTa-OzaPWdxHDL4GzwPkZ0rceDQmcW4vAmdNqWeBMDC0Ist2fBfYECI5KBbZ5I_hboEVCTcDxIAgpA0q8AurGmguKPUuXjX9_InMsehRKbi8b-f-W-rMHD4P_AgAA___B1Ybf) of _U.S. News & World Report's_ national rankings of the best large cities to live in, earning the No. 2 spot for 2025-2026. The publication evaluated cities with populations above 500,000 on factors including quality of life, value, desirability, job market, and migration. El Paso's combination of affordable housing, low median rent, and livability [set it apart](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2O6yAUhJ8GdycCjCEuKG7jLrfd0uLn2D4KgchmneTtV-wrbDPNSJ_mm6_bfHOUKK__3QNtfS9lzvg6EtaK-4zp6Y6Si_S0Bqqf3VGmvHo3Sy41cAVcz9FR-syqi9bzOIoOrTBmUKaXY99tFk3gix7F9aoHHozwYjA6jL0QIXhvVEe2wbjiWggu5HiJEVXPwzL0HhePmimOkWrZL3XDim93LOlTTtwvoTy6ZLdanwfr_zE5MTndT3KtYHJqJkxODc_kxFWLgckJEzQv2F2-Y4RcQILHo0Jy-4rQTKEWSHQiUIa6IXxDI3W7jc8XpUSHNkzx9eEo_a6of_vutPInAAD__6GvgQE) from most of the country's largest metros. "_This moment speaks to who we are as a city and where we are headed_ ," said Mayor Renard U. Johnson. City Manager Dionne Mack added that the recognition "_reinforces the strengths that continue to make El Paso a place people are proud to call home_ ," pointing to ongoing city investments in infrastructure, public safety, economic mobility, and quality of life. Texas cities [dominated the rankings](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL1uhDAQhJ8GOpAxtoHCRZrrLm1KtOCFW2XPRvbmft4-Iq-QbopPM5rv6zpfgZji_gl39PLa0hzxWRhFMM_IB5QUk15oX0neGShS3BeYtdKuUaZRbg5A_J5NHfyiwtTV6LthsGbo9dTXNx-c08aawSpwU4c42nEct34NEKydFNTkzzJllOs61empDQFNr9bN9gtuC7rKKAwkKbdyQ8EXlI3f6YG5XdO9Zn8TOUrVf1T6UulLRmAsAoLtTzm_nFSlLwfDiuUEIH5T3M-4YJGGIe_YrCSEpc4-HE9ipuKGyqj9DsR_M_I_OQ-vfwMAAP__vNV6TQ), with five cracking the top 10. Austin came in at No. 3, Fort Worth at No. 4, San Antonio at No. 6, and Houston at No. 10. Oklahoma City was ranked No. 1.
## Texas Leads in Affordable, Fast-Growing Cities
Texas topped all 50 states with 11 cities ranked among the most affordable and fastest-growing in the country, according to a [new study by MoneyLion](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD3O4yAUAE-DO1vwwHYoKFZaucu2W1r8PGwkbCJ4iZPbr7JX-OqRZqT5e1_vNuV0bn_sgYbesawnXi0jEdYV88O2chZwafOJPtWmM52bsytwmHquej6twab8WVUXjONBiw6NmOdRzRK07HYjndYgQHuPN5iViPoWJgtuEqMfRxi7ZL4yrvgkBBeghxBQSe7jKB1GhxNTHEOiUgfakfBtW8yf8sI6-HJ02exEj8bkLwYLg-W6rsGW_GUMFlsp-YyNwTLy_iiNehtjqcG6jH20jbBRv9VypXPrBXDO9azmYacjM7lsT-_L8ySsTP4WXTXhcaWcU5tmpvh22PQ_1NHP1r0M_AsAAP__YfaCmQ). Florida was second with seven qualifying cities. To be included, cities had to have total populations of at least 100,000 residents, one-year and five-year population growth rates above the national average, and rental or mortgage costs below the national average. MoneyLion used the U.S. Census, Zillow, and Bureau of Labor Statistics expenditure data to find where affordability and growth still intersect, drawing on the Census American Community Survey data from 2019, 2023, and 2024 to calculate population change and leftover savings for both homeowners and renters. Texas cities [claimed four of the top 12 spots](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLuOwyAQAL_G7rAA41dBcU26XHultZjFWQlDBJs4-ftT7heuH81I83Ndr0CR0v4NB1p-hbwmPGtEZiwrxjvUnLJ2tG_E7wKUKO0OVi31KKQRclw9UHyvpvXWSb-oFq2apsFMvV769mbBbM7JYTCwzH7Ts_I-gJezhmHQ_exbsh-ZNHJUSiq9dN6j6eUWht5hcDg2RqInzqXjGzK-oIb4zk8s3ZaPNtob8702_VejL42-nOfZcYEnRkg-ItVHwQ_Y6MuRKwsIIRcPLqIIUBkri73kk9IuNmLCKh4VhFJLPy6Dbov195NipDpOjZH7ART_uvy_W0-rfwMAAP__4h6A2Q) on the national list, with Frisco taking the No. 1 overall ranking, followed by New Braunfels at No. 3, McKinney at No. 4, and Allen at No. 6. League City, Conroe, Lewisville, Pearland, Denton, Fort Worth, and Grand Prairie rounded out the Texas contingent. Peter,
We wish there was better news today. But here's the bottom line, and a reality we need to be ready for:
Virginia's redistricting campaign is in serious trouble. Democrats could lose this important push to gain up to 5 additional blue seats.
With a little over two weeks left before Election Day in VA, early vote stats and new polling show Democrats are facing a tough uphill battle. MAGA voters are reportedly much more eager to turn out and defeat the ballot measure than Democrats are to fight to win.
If MAGA can overcome the odds in VA to defeat the Dem-backed redistricting proposal mere months after Democrats swept statewide elections with winning margins between 7 and 15 points, the tide will have fully turned against us in the redistricting war.
And our backs will be up against the wall here in Colorado at the exact moment our proposal to redraw CO's map will be progressing to a vote...

Last week, Oracle laid off about 30,000 workers, approximately 18% of its global workforce. Simultaneously, Oracle is planning to invest $50 billion in AI infrastructure development this year alone.
This is tectonic. Those 30,000 workers cost about $8 billion a year. The message is clear - fewer human salaries, more data centers. The amount of money spent on building data centers recently surpassed the amount of money spent on [office](https://substack.com/redirect/23beecc1-76a9-476d-9eb0-62fdf501dd6e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) buildings for the first time.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ee8637a6-3703-462b-8ef5-7e11f0923bc8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

The server farm is the new human.
Also last week, OpenAI announced it was raising $122 billion at a staggering $852 billion valuation, the heftiest raise for a private company in history. This seemed like an incredible vote of confidence in its business.
But if you dug a little deeper, you'd see that the vast majority of this $122 billion - $110 billion - came from only 3 companies: Amazon with $50 billion, Nvidia for $30 billion, and SoftBank for $30 billion. These companies are all already massive investors and partners to OpenAI - they need it to succeed for their own sakes. Only $12 billion came from other entities and individuals, including Microsoft which has already invested billions in OpenAI.
This reminded me of a business joke: "If I owe you one million dollars, I'm in trouble. If I owe you a billion dollars... you're in trouble."
Microsoft, Nvidia and SoftBank are so deep in hock to OpenAI that they need it to succeed.
OpenAI recently abandoned its much-hyped Sora AI-for-video offering despite high-profile partnerships with Disney and other media companies. There wasn't that much demand, but the costs of the computing resources for Sora were at least a million dollars a day. Hence, they pulled the plug.
Instead, last week OpenAI acquired the technology YouTube / X show TBPN. I appeared on TBPN a few months ago to talk about Noble Mobile. Why is an AI company acquiring a new media channel for hundreds of millions of dollars?
It's a great question. The answer, in my mind, clearly seems to be to try and shape the narrative among techies around AI and OpenAI.
It's not a normal business practice and it doesn't make much sense in a normal world; if your business is AI, why buy a media mouthpiece? That's... just weird.
Of course, if your stock is now valued at $852 billion, you can spend a couple hundred million on some YouTubers / X broadcasters without it being too big a deal.
But still, I find this to be something that raises more questions than it answers.
OpenAI touted its massive revenue growth - up to $2 billion a month. ChatGPT remains dominant among non-business users even as OpenAI is trying to gain traction with companies.
OpenAI's competitor, Anthropic, is now preparing to go public in one of the biggest IPOs ever. The folks I know use 'Claude' as shorthand for their ass-kicking colleague in the enterprise setting. This is where OpenAI wants to be.
What are the takeaways? First, the scale of investment in AI is now so breathtaking that people are just incidental costs. Data centers are the new offices. [Layoffs](https://substack.com/redirect/3cabddcd-02d8-4709-95bf-9629f37fcac0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) are the go-to move for big companies trying to take advantage of AI and will only pick up steam.
Second, in order for OpenAI to justify its new valuation, it will need to increase revenue by an additional tens of billions of dollars, which suggests to me that either it's going to replace a huge chunk of the workforce, or it's going to fall short of its current projections. Or maybe both.
Finally, OpenAI is the new 'too big to fail' company, similar to the big banks during the mortgage meltdown. Of course, the banks wound up with the federal government as a backstop. If OpenAI ever needs the Feds to step in... the market will be in big trouble.
None of this is good news. Be prepared for strange - and tough - times for people ahead.

Derek,
As the DNC’s Executive Director, it’s my job to guide our Party’s long-term strategy.
So, as we look ahead to the midterms, here’s a quick update for you:
Democrats need to flip **four** Republican seats to take control of the Senate this November. That means winning races in states like Texas, North Carolina, Ohio, and Alaska. To take back the House, we need to hold the seats we have and flip at least three more.
**This operation is going to take a _massive_ amount of resources. Trust me, our team is crunching the numbers every day.**
But we also know how to win tough races. That’s why at the DNC, we’re making unprecedented investments in voter registration and state parties. And we’re working to reach voters who may have sat out previous elections.
We’re doing everything we can to make sure we take back Congress — but to make sure we’re on track to win, we have to meet our fundraising goals. Unfortunately, we’re not quite on track right now.

To Donald Trump, America is “too big” to take care of our own people.
#

Peter,
To Donald Trump, America is “too big” to take care of our own people.
[](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/1000?c0=ruben-em-apr26.ZLvc4O&refcode=em260406-1-90&t=1&akid=4111%2E734936%2EsGXCX9)
To him, America would be great if everyone was too afraid to oppose him. America would be truly great, to Trump, if the entire world feared us. Trump thinks sending American kids to die in a war makes this country great, and makes him look strong.
But to me, he’s just a small man with small hands doing a job that’s way too big for him.
America will be great when parents don’t have to choose between dinner and medication. When kids are safe in their schools, when they can get a great education, and graduate into a world full of opportunities. When people don’t have to be scared that they’ll have to work until they die, and can retire with dignity and security.
If you ask me, that’s an America worth fighting for. We can make some progress towards that future this year, but I can’t do it alone.

clean_body: To Donald Trump, America is “too big” to take care of our own people. Peter, To Donald Trump, America is “too big” to take care of our own people. To him, America would be great if everyone was too afraid to oppose him. America would be truly great, to Trump, if the entire world feared us. Trump thinks sending American kids to die in a war makes this country great, and makes him look strong. But to me, he’s just a small man with small hands doing a job that’s way too big for him. America will be great when parents don’t have to choose between dinner and medication. When kids are safe in their schools, when they can get a great education, and graduate into a world full of opportunities. When people don’t have to be scared that they’ll have to work until they die, and can retire with dignity and security. If you ask me, that’s an America worth fighting for. We can make some progress towards that future this year, but I can’t do it alone. Friends,
Please save the date for a special evening in support of Republican candidates in the U.S. Virgin Islands.
**RPVI Fundraiser Reception****May 29th, 2026****6:00pm - 9:00pm****Private Villa on St. Thomas (location details to follow)**
Join us for a gathering featuring a distinguished guest speaker, hosted at a stunning private villa on St. Thomas. This reception will raise critical funds to support our efforts to elect Republican candidates in the upcoming elections including races for the Virgin Islands Senate, Congress, and the Governor's office.
Now more than ever, it is essential that we have a strong Republican voice in our local government. Your attendance and support will make a direct impact on our ability to field and back quality candidates across the territory.
Additional details including the venue address, featured speaker, and ticket information will be shared in the coming weeks. For now, please mark your calendar and plan to be with us on May 29th.
Thank you for your continued commitment to RPVI and to the future of the Virgin Islands.
Warm regards,
April NewlandNational Committeewoman Representing the U.S. Virgin Islands

name: Marsha Blackburn
subject: Never expected to get the cold shoulder from YOU
body:
Peter, why have you been giving us the cold shoulder?
I know I've reached out this week about this issue.My team tells me they've texted and emailed at least twice too!

# **US Air Force colonel evaded capture for 36 hours in Iran 's Zagros Mountains despite serious injuries and $60,000 bounty**
A seriously wounded US Air Force colonel climbed a 7,000-foot ridge and hid in a crevice in Iran's Zagros Mountains for 36 hours after his F-15E was shot down Friday, **[evading"thousands of these savages"](https://substack.com/redirect/ad075035-6bae-41d3-a75c-99630e29fe3b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** hunting him down for a $60,000 bounty, President Trump told Axios. Armed only with a handgun, the weapons officer climbed more than 1.3 miles and sent an emergency beacon from a mountain crevice early Sunday, though Trump initially feared the signal could be a trap.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ad075035-6bae-41d3-a75c-99630e29fe3b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Why it matters:** The officer submitted an unusual radio message saying "God is good" before extraction, which "sounded like something a Muslim would say," Trump said, referencing the Islamic phrase "Allahu Akbar." A massive daylight operation involving 100 Special Operations forces led by Seal Team 6, dozens of aircraft, and MQ-9 Reaper drones providing a 2-mile protective perimeter successfully rescued him, with the CIA planting fake intel that he'd already escaped. Two aircraft became stuck, forcing the US to destroy trapped vehicles.
* **The operation:** The complex rescue involved Delta Force commandos and Army Rangers on standby, with special ops engaging in skirmishes with local tribesmen. The officer's pilot was rescued hours after the crash, while the colonel was flown to Kuwait for medical treatment. War Secretary Pete Hegseth posted "God is good" on X after the rescue.

# **Trump says U.S. forces will hit Iran "extremely hard" over next several weeks if strait not open by Tuesday**
President Trump said Wednesday the war with Iran is "nearing completion" and "we're getting very close," **[warning U.S. forces will"hit them extremely hard](https://substack.com/redirect/26f90414-0f54-4e72-8d80-5774c3cc7f0a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** over the next two to three weeks" and "bring them back to the Stone Ages." Trump gave Iran until Tuesday to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, warning failure could trigger sweeping strikes on energy infrastructure, saying "if no deal is made... we are going to hit each and every one of their electric-generating plants, very hard and probably simultaneously."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/26f90414-0f54-4e72-8d80-5774c3cc7f0a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Why it matters:** The U.S. has begun expanding targets to include major infrastructure, striking one of Iran's largest bridges--a critical transportation artery--with Trump writing "the biggest bridge in Iran comes tumbling down, never to be used again -- Much more to follow! IT IS TIME FOR IRAN TO MAKE A DEAL BEFORE IT IS TOO LATE." Military analysts say "finishing the job" is unlikely to be a single strike but rather escalating options from attacking remaining missile/drone networks to broader infrastructure strikes, though critics like Quincy Institute's Trita Parsi said Trump's address "reveals that he doesn't have a plan."
* **The uncertainty:** Recent U.S. intelligence suggests roughly half of Iran's missile launchers remain intact with thousands of drones still in its arsenal, though Trump may rely on continuous surveillance of nuclear sites rather than ground operations to seize enriched uranium. The influx of thousands of troops from Marine Expeditionary Units and 82nd Airborne has fueled speculation about ground operations to seize Kharg Island or recover over 400 kilograms of highly enriched uranium entombed in Isfahan's tunnel complex since the U.S. collapsed entrances in June 2025.

"Today" show host Savannah Guthrie **[delivered a deeply emotional Easter message](https://substack.com/redirect/f7a2fefb-a1a1-46ed-9ca5-7c6426df48ed?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** reflecting on faith, doubt, and uncertainty as her 84-year-old mother, Nancy Guthrie, remains missing after 63 days.
"There are moments in which that promise seems irretrievably far away, when life itself seems far harder than death," Guthrie said. "These moments of deep disappointment with God, the feeling of utter abandonment."

"It is the darkness that makes this morning's light so magnificent, so blindingly beautiful," she said, concluding "I still believe. And so I say with conviction, happy Easter."

subject: BREITBART: BILL CASSIDY BACKED DEI BUREAUCRACY ACROSS 4 MAJOR SENATE VOTES
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Julia Letlow for Louisiana
body:
Sen. Bill Cassidy's record of supporting major legislation that funded diversity, equity, and inclusion programs has emerged as a central issue

| | |
---
| | | | [|
---](https://julialetlow.us19.list-manage.com/track/click?u=70758973fc60553eda6683b43&id=e054b294c3&e=95355a072c)
| | | | | | **BREITBART: BILL CASSIDY BACKED DEI BUREAUCRACY ACROSS 4 MAJOR SENATE VOTES**
_Sen. Bill Cassidy’s record of supporting major legislation that funded diversity, equity, and inclusion programs has emerged as a central issue in Louisiana’s 2026 Republican Senate primary, where Trump-endorsed Rep. Julia Letlow and Louisiana Treasurer John Fleming are challenging Cassidy._
[_**BREITBART**_](https://julialetlow.us19.list-manage.com/track/click?u=70758973fc60553eda6683b43&id=1524622c45&e=95355a072c) _**| Jasmyn Jordan | April 2, 2026**_
---
|
---
| | | | | | Cassidy voted for four major pieces of legislation that created federal diversity offices, embedded equity requirements, and, in some cases, funded programs later canceled or identified by the Trump administration as DEI initiatives: the Fiscal Year 2021 National Defense Authorization Act, the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, the CHIPS and Science Act, and the Safer Communities Act.
Cassidy voted for final passage of the FY2021 National Defense Authorization Act and later voted to override President Donald Trump’s veto. The bill created Chief Diversity Officers for the Department of the Navy, Department of the Air Force, and the Coast Guard. It also established a Department of Defense Diversity and Inclusion Advisory Council.
Cassidy also played a leading role in writing and [passing](https://julialetlow.us19.list-manage.com/track/click?u=70758973fc60553eda6683b43&id=a5e49a88cd&e=95355a072c) the $1.2 trillion Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act. Cassidy was one of the original ten senators who negotiated the bill and became its most prominent Republican advocate.
The infrastructure package included several equity-related provisions. It created the $2.75 billion Digital Equity Act, which directed broadband funding under criteria tied to race and identity. It also incorporated the Biden administration’s Justice40 initiative, requiring 40 percent of infrastructure benefits to flow to disadvantaged communities under an equity framework. In addition, the legislation provided $3.5 billion for direct air capture hubs with climate equity requirements attached to the funding.
The Biden administration later [promoted](https://julialetlow.us19.list-manage.com/track/click?u=70758973fc60553eda6683b43&id=c737ec1b3a&e=95355a072c) the infrastructure bill as “an opportunity to advance equity in our country.” Cassidy did not merely vote for the bill after it was written; he helped negotiate and draft the legislation that included those provisions from the outset.
Cassidy also [voted](https://julialetlow.us19.list-manage.com/track/click?u=70758973fc60553eda6683b43&id=016c1bcd85&e=95355a072c) for the $280 billion CHIPS and Science Act, which passed the Senate 64-33. The law directed the Government Accountability Office to inventory federal research programs aimed at minority-serving institutions, added diversity-related requirements throughout the federal science funding framework, and created a Chief Diversity Officer position at the National Science Foundation.
After the bill became law, the Biden Commerce Department imposed additional diversity and equity requirements on CHIPS funding recipients. Cassidy later criticized those regulations in a letter to the Commerce Department, arguing that the administration had added burdensome requirements. But the law Cassidy voted for had already created a Chief Diversity Officer at the National Science Foundation and included other diversity-focused mandates in federal research funding.
Cassidy was one of the original ten Republican framework negotiators [behind](https://julialetlow.us19.list-manage.com/track/click?u=70758973fc60553eda6683b43&id=afc0afbb47&e=95355a072c) the Safer Communities Act and one of only 15 Senate Republicans to vote for final passage of the bill.
The legislation included $750 million for state crisis intervention programs, $1 billion for school safety, and $250 million for community-based violence prevention initiatives. The Trump administration later canceled the community violence prevention grants, explicitly labeling them DEI vehicles.
Cassidy backed each of those four bills while also distancing himself from President Trump.
In February 2021, Cassidy [voted](https://julialetlow.us19.list-manage.com/track/click?u=70758973fc60553eda6683b43&id=0fdcd52d70&e=95355a072c) to convict Trump during the Senate impeachment trial following the January 6 Capitol riot. After the vote, Cassidy said, “I voted to convict President Trump because he is guilty.”
Cassidy [continued](https://julialetlow.us19.list-manage.com/track/click?u=70758973fc60553eda6683b43&id=5ec75b7f8b&e=95355a072c) to distance himself from Trump after the impeachment vote. In October 2021, he said he would not vote for Trump in the 2024 presidential election and argued that Trump could not win another general election after Republicans lost the House, Senate, and White House during Trump’s first term. Cassidy said, “President Trump is the first president, on the Republican side at least, to lose the House, the Senate and the presidency in four years.” When asked whether he would vote for Trump, Cassidy responded, “I’m not.”
Cassidy [repeated](https://julialetlow.us19.list-manage.com/track/click?u=70758973fc60553eda6683b43&id=aa8d345a20&e=95355a072c) that argument in May 2023, saying Trump could not defeat Joe Biden in a general election and pointing to Republican losses in the 2022 midterm elections.
In August 2023, Cassidy [said](https://julialetlow.us19.list-manage.com/track/click?u=70758973fc60553eda6683b43&id=c763438e0b&e=95355a072c) Trump should leave the 2024 race. When asked whether Trump should step aside, Cassidy responded, “I think so.” One month later, Cassidy [signaled](https://julialetlow.us19.list-manage.com/track/click?u=70758973fc60553eda6683b43&id=e6e0b6f22c&e=95355a072c) openness to supporting or joining a No Labels third-party effort rather than backing Trump, saying, “If they came and spoke to me, I would certainly speak to them back.”

Peter,

You may already know who I am from my basketball career. Or, maybe you’re just hearing about me for the first time through my Senate Campaign. Either way, I wanted to formally introduce myself and share my story. [**_Afterward, I’m going to ask you to send a small contribution to my campaign as I continue to fight to Flip Minnesota Red._**](https://links.iterable.com/u/click?_t=ce1ce9e616484205a28a45cfaf96cecf&_m=08d5f9f0592b4a28aca273810914dba8&_e=56YNyCGnqjOvX2u0vtmpVLEI7UZnBo9N4QT8DurQl5wOSdFUGoWqKmgvYjJJKLzEWuArwyKv-s7qrj7cjssPZhk90_ff6PyPWAywHj79Zowr4fzOtuAo49FsJ2o6Ei5eWges_xW-DHda63-6jpwoVEw1h7MuX4gec57rU-FoZxNeSNIkLC7cnyhWS9JDXuplejmxIOa5gfTu-_qz9BwKB8YxSrfSOUhaSDWu-5lV97jsSUDT2WbXW-nfGPcerwRf5CR0jjlO61LhykQCyWV4RvnWHXF5GdKGETg9sXkjGOHE-CtdKPZo7A89d-_adR-jdOQA9JgRY2bUYdMyZ6rV9lsdFG-LhTFwHNDhzs-xxxdcOGzJylqk-UWcH2D0xJHX2Oxuu3Ja-Fm5HbpTDSiCM3yPwwOddBsIYY-AHAPdYSXZbzmVizSuXh8Mx86DkDALzV-lDpqlDd2KaHfZ1hAnnUdqV5TJ_HY9YXABW6-Cts5AAkhKbzJoPNORJdoPhB_NEv0TxILIOngMLYz14clbwqDhzU_rwds_yYQH3uR_RYQfCgQg5mbWkeCpKl6GYkMU)

I was born and raised in the Twin Cities in Minnesota, mainly in the Rondo Community of St. Paul. At the age of five, I started playing sports, and at nine years old, I was already playing basketball on the Northside of Minneapolis. My mother was a single mother who worked tirelessly to give me a better life. I went to school in Rondo and began to excel at basketball. By 10th grade, I was ranked as a top 20 player in the country. I remember dreaming of reaching the NBA one day– a dream shared by millions of kids.

[](https://links.iterable.com/u/click?_t=ce1ce9e616484205a28a45cfaf96cecf&_m=08d5f9f0592b4a28aca273810914dba8&_e=56YNyCGnqjOvX2u0vtmpVLEI7UZnBo9N4QT8DurQl5wOSdFUGoWqKmgvYjJJKLzEWuArwyKv-s7qrj7cjssPZhk90_ff6PyPWAywHj79Zowr4fzOtuAo49FsJ2o6Ei5eWges_xW-DHda63-6jpwoVEw1h7MuX4gec57rU-FoZxNeSNIkLC7cnyhWS9JDXupl7hieGERfO0UARHcWVo3ihb5vqUXppIpf75ifrBOiomI0px9MwGO6L8f8EtdetsXvils-ol4nJZfiFtPeJa0aSpq2SKX0tVcgjqS6QngZUKo2njj39fO9hlNyl95fb7McetpNGRbUzKXr6msneORZRIv53xEtFQVPd1dYzlj1IkM-sUXEvY63TONJs1GlGaQrihLdg4I6ZfPDcmZ2GSKRSt6UlwmbbLIrOuZern5VX2gDmInf2hto8Bm60c-OwCkxYSipT8CpzgNfVQy43ZTzIsXPMyEecLYi_KYP-WtJPrFPgRr7gkOmivL14bYee6IvLUtjXXp8lP7mFynYsYLZnqRXGby8SkNe7QXIb4J00PW_h6LRmeaglJhhaNdlphiG)
I accepted a scholarship at the University of Minnesota, but shortly after transferred to Iowa State. There, I won multiple basketball awards while working hard in class and being named on the Dean’s List for academics.

[](https://links.iterable.com/u/click?_t=ce1ce9e616484205a28a45cfaf96cecf&_m=08d5f9f0592b4a28aca273810914dba8&_e=56YNyCGnqjOvX2u0vtmpVLEI7UZnBo9N4QT8DurQl5wOSdFUGoWqKmgvYjJJKLzEWuArwyKv-s7qrj7cjssPZhk90_ff6PyPWAywHj79Zowr4fzOtuAo49FsJ2o6Ei5eWges_xW-DHda63-6jpwoVEw1h7MuX4gec57rU-FoZxNeSNIkLC7cnyhWS9JDXupldKw17HvT0-iZt7OMfjqRa5rGoOmC8UV8uUYyzsPPyxY5WhRoRavJ1bOLdedjrhKGMnwk8fBAG2WQF-Kh00gbI79UVrOPQe6y-gXdeHVlMIqX47X4eec4oq7QHoNolYYThQKLHU-5Gmhkfh3m938JLN09MYolJ15pHzmzpcUgG-FaF3yQSUK9AT2VO4pEaTq-D3dlLalljtjjxmnr6lAV1tsfaMBd4366UJtZNU9Bm6OsKdai3-GPhFGSPtNfYPS1CekoIxSyieH8q0hEiEKw_uCpOXJ9E-wKn6xWDW3mupu8QlHoaDmNsYwov_nvHodxO7pXo_Rn0cv6PgU7oG2zij-HNWDTYk-64PhDQ_ksWa4lMDDeb2SiJa0nT_J1Ry3N)
Finally, my dream came true. I was selected in the first round of the 2012 NBA Draft, going to the Houston Rockets. While playing at the highest level of basketball competition in the world, I began to voice concerns about the NBA’s Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA), specifically regarding mental health policy, which at the time did not exist.

Eventually, my concerns became a dispute between the NBA and myself, until I demanded that the NBA spearhead the mental health conversation through policy. This led to the end of my NBA career, but my work led to the NBA implementing policies to support players’ mental health.

[](https://links.iterable.com/u/click?_t=ce1ce9e616484205a28a45cfaf96cecf&_m=08d5f9f0592b4a28aca273810914dba8&_e=56YNyCGnqjOvX2u0vtmpVLEI7UZnBo9N4QT8DurQl5wOSdFUGoWqKmgvYjJJKLzEWuArwyKv-s7qrj7cjssPZhk90_ff6PyPWAywHj79Zowr4fzOtuAo49FsJ2o6Ei5eWges_xW-DHda63-6jpwoVEw1h7MuX4gec57rU-FoZxNeSNIkLC7cnyhWS9JDXupl3rv93g7D7ts3AdyNddTs573Q-qWr10tfZGfWpPhDskQ2hqIp7F3_QAM6ild2-SPUhEpkXkGnqRKYAuyeGrCl5sgP4qfeuEnUhbsMdvqh1cm--wMsOob6bgoe9HfZW3rxIpya1WfZox3KvCv83GKyECViLP7fvFi_upIs_w6XuTnJFQyDkH338S7UdE00c5QV1oGXLYIWnfwT-OnKXduVBfje4PzcJNWvU3teoJLUTfs97LXzUWtYz5CPbc28IoZHKQx98oirltbdwMZDldm9edhBINicriNEF1vWsZAicvppv-fNVENc6iJ4Txf6dplYx31qLbLshGqk3a_5cELnB9Lm0hGFeh_d3xM9jew0WiOdqzUKIsQJK_aNq0xR6XkZ)
I gave up my dream of playing in the NBA to stand up for something I fully believe in. That experience gave me the courage to run for Congress in 2022 and for Senate in 2024. More on that later.

After leaving the NBA, I took my talents to Canada, playing professional basketball and winning two championships. Then, I joined the BIG 3 Basketball Tournament, a professional 3 on 3 league; I still play today.

[](https://links.iterable.com/u/click?_t=ce1ce9e616484205a28a45cfaf96cecf&_m=08d5f9f0592b4a28aca273810914dba8&_e=56YNyCGnqjOvX2u0vtmpVLEI7UZnBo9N4QT8DurQl5wOSdFUGoWqKmgvYjJJKLzEWuArwyKv-s7qrj7cjssPZhk90_ff6PyPWAywHj79Zowr4fzOtuAo49FsJ2o6Ei5eWges_xW-DHda63-6jpwoVEw1h7MuX4gec57rU-FoZxNeSNIkLC7cnyhWS9JDXuplwPITH6kyWBL275oheps8hyBB3dXuP8jZL9051EH7pchRIGlXjxA_oCDU1zQoDNPKWKk4LBAR-8LkqMBL3AdtwoNE5_R3AFyw0DNTpoxT1FeJCE-fhQW009lPHxGYIXn0LJiLWHGOwkoMfFFJEYwhRinhMfVkdCzQkh4i10sqUwz3eDDUPp_FYqdtdywEOb9Cn8RW_BX9qERb1AeovQDmdorx-ADAvatTbdFM8A7hGcp2wHukyibQ4Ml2dAtwBm-S9wKdJHgx9xmCWa4gSRsxrlL5wNOmuwc7wCkrA9uiiFoimsmRVIBrnSBvXvS1Zeo9FjLwtMA7UGammH4z3gU8Cs7WYrLF03t2bg1N4EfcQh9A5wt_vYXsPyeQIXSvmsbp)
It was at this point that I became increasingly vocal about standing up for the core principles that I believe in. I’ve continued to be outspoken on taboo subjects, like freeing the Uyghurs, the Federal Reserve, Julian Assange, Edward Snowden, Muammar Gaddafi, and many others. **I’m not afraid to speak up and say the silent part out loud. I will never just shut up and dribble.**

In 2022, I decided to run for Congress against Radical Leftist and Squad Founder, Ilhan Omar. The Deep State Democrats lined her pocket with millions of dollars to beat me, and I came up short.

[](https://links.iterable.com/u/click?_t=ce1ce9e616484205a28a45cfaf96cecf&_m=08d5f9f0592b4a28aca273810914dba8&_e=56YNyCGnqjOvX2u0vtmpVLEI7UZnBo9N4QT8DurQl5wOSdFUGoWqKmgvYjJJKLzEWuArwyKv-s7qrj7cjssPZhk90_ff6PyPWAywHj79Zowr4fzOtuAo49FsJ2o6Ei5eWges_xW-DHda63-6jpwoVEw1h7MuX4gec57rU-FoZxNeSNIkLC7cnyhWS9JDXupleZiAt0mLu2Zht_MIm5zNkSnLqsfscS-ZIny1KcVKPCaw0xH_P1FWXLmfkMWr_bR4vz8C8wUOpB0dj4xrybXp-bP99UkG1tlOS3xgqXfXXeDLid1nHL_cjVSkIMbpR1q9JWtPqT3yIapeWJxuSHukELltroJOIZf7nyntBtXEb49kA8WYabVVFLIqXGw-p8ERVqzeQLgcDUM8t9dYtBE_nCjRAd6-BQufdCy1bG-wLEHuSr5ZDKWfv1oafYV1nvONEecVAviR4gRNTFRnHf_UwEjOHbqGoKXbvHBd9Ghkrk5ATSTNIevVgBqDCjnDWRG7KXz4AeeSOxxXb8iVMhJmD5Cr1DdkDfMGFlbdWR5Si2_UTcIuwlpUk1CvZ53IYbak)
Now, I’m running for United States Senate to defeat RINO Michele Tafoya. She represents the Establishment who would rather see America become the next Communist China or Soviet Russia. The Industrial Media Complex will continue to spread false narratives claiming that I have little chance of winning. But they continue to ignore my strong grassroots movement with the American People, who are sick and tired of being overstepped, ignored, and told to accept the policies that our Liberal Leaders force down our throats.

We CAN win, but it’s going to take the help of a huge grassroots movement. That’s why I’m emailing you today, Peter. We have a chance to make history by electing the youngest US Senator and the first one born in the 1990s.

[**I am humbly asking you to send my campaign a small donation of whatever you can afford. Whether it’s $5, $15, or $25, every single donation makes a difference.**](https://links.iterable.com/u/click?_t=ce1ce9e616484205a28a45cfaf96cecf&_m=08d5f9f0592b4a28aca273810914dba8&_e=56YNyCGnqjOvX2u0vtmpVLEI7UZnBo9N4QT8DurQl5wOSdFUGoWqKmgvYjJJKLzEWuArwyKv-s7qrj7cjssPZhk90_ff6PyPWAywHj79Zowr4fzOtuAo49FsJ2o6Ei5eWges_xW-DHda63-6jpwoVEw1h7MuX4gec57rU-FoZxNeSNIkLC7cnyhWS9JDXuplaDNlIIkqNaeCHn4V5DOFCtE4cFNT_bdaF8LqOth-IowBaRsFDogjQy7l8qO7BFXqY4gkJcl95-z26AbeEg1EszwhOAEq0LACSCbdAwvYpUwusRDX8KRsMl2GVMMSQ5345EsQfOmreuQp12gDOapU3QQg7gRAp1aiwfrEgiQtxHu86wB4EWjEVrs4JZ5bMvSlBF5X27a8ncBBniHUVrJqzhKvo7ng7EIUOTPdjIjSWFuGNNGh7slHaf2sADQS6akh09L338kO05y8dgr01W78k2sONMxqcv_Ubix-rRTxJamWmMp0F-BHljjkOTixYCT-PpgmdyGxVtSiklTsfmJiOrK7U4gqThv_2yLf4hXraAoCZiAUmG3cCDF0tFst7E8l)

I’m looking forward to getting to know you better, and I hope you’ll join my team.

Either way, I wanted to formally introduce myself and share my story. I was born and raised in the Twin Cities in Minnesota, mainly in the Rondo Community of St. Paul. At the age of five, I started playing sports, and at nine years old, I was already playing basketball on the Northside of Minneapolis. My mother was a single mother who worked tirelessly to give me a better life. I went to school in Rondo and began to excel at basketball. By 10th grade, I was ranked as a top 20 player in the country. I remember dreaming of reaching the NBA one day– a dream shared by millions of kids. I accepted a scholarship at the University of Minnesota, but shortly after transferred to Iowa State. There, I won multiple basketball awards while working hard in class and being named on the Dean’s List for academics. Finally, my dream came true. I was selected in the first round of the 2012 NBA Draft, going to the Houston Rockets. While playing at the highest level of basketball competition in the world, I began to voice concerns about the NBA’s Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA), specifically regarding mental health policy, which at the time did not exist. Eventually, my concerns became a dispute between the NBA and myself, until I demanded that the NBA spearhead the mental health conversation through policy. This led to the end of my NBA career, but my work led to the NBA implementing policies to support players’ mental health. I gave up my dream of playing in the NBA to stand up for something I fully believe in. That experience gave me the courage to run for Congress in 2022 and for Senate in 2024. More on that later. After leaving the NBA, I took my talents to Canada, playing professional basketball and winning two championships. Then, I joined the BIG 3 Basketball Tournament, a professional 3 on 3 league; I still play today. It was at this point that I became increasingly vocal about standing up for the core principles that I believe in. I’ve continued to be outspoken on taboo subjects, like freeing the Uyghurs, the Federal Reserve, Julian Assange, Edward Snowden, Muammar Gaddafi, and many others. I’m not afraid to speak up and say the silent part out loud. I will never just shut up and dribble. In 2022, I decided to run for Congress against Radical Leftist and Squad Founder, Ilhan Omar. The Deep State Democrats lined her pocket with millions of dollars to beat me, and I came up short. Now, I’m running for United States Senate to defeat RINO Michele Tafoya. She represents the Establishment who would rather see America become the next Communist China or Soviet Russia. The Industrial Media Complex will continue to spread false narratives claiming that I have little chance of winning. But they continue to ignore my strong grassroots movement with the American People, who are sick and tired of being overstepped, ignored, and told to accept the policies that our Liberal Leaders force down our throats. We CAN win, but it’s going to take the help of a huge grassroots movement. That’s why I’m emailing you today, Peter. We have a chance to make history by electing the youngest US Senator and the first one born in the 1990s. I’m looking forward to getting to know you better, and I hope you’ll join my team. Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | First Invеstmеnt Updаtеs brоught tо уоu bу Іnception Media, LLC. | Dear Peter,

Imagine you're pregnant in Georgia, and you've decided what kind of care you want—the care of a midwife you trust and who listens—someone you want by your side through one of the most vulnerable moments of your life. [And then you find out: the law doesn’t care what you want.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/128903767/612654933/-107964346?sourceid=1151260&utm_campaign=midwives&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=midwives&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI0YTczYzFjOC1jZjMxLWYxMTEtOWE0OC0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=y-DMr6-fbY398qKNiOdIIaYBI-nrJXUdyspGgckPmNw=&emci=c22d22c1-cf31-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&emdi=4a73c1c8-cf31-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&ceid=954237)

Families across Georgia are living this reality—in a state with some of the worst maternal health outcomes in the country and laws that treat midwives like criminals.

[We're suing the state of Georgia to change that.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/128903768/612654934/-107964346?sourceid=1151260&utm_campaign=midwives&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=midwives&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI0YTczYzFjOC1jZjMxLWYxMTEtOWE0OC0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=y-DMr6-fbY398qKNiOdIIaYBI-nrJXUdyspGgckPmNw=&emci=c22d22c1-cf31-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&emdi=4a73c1c8-cf31-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&ceid=954237) | [MIDWIVES SAVE LIVES](https://click.everyaction.com/k/128903769/612654935/-107964346?sourceid=1151260&utm_campaign=midwives&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=midwives&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI0YTczYzFjOC1jZjMxLWYxMTEtOWE0OC0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=y-DMr6-fbY398qKNiOdIIaYBI-nrJXUdyspGgckPmNw=&emci=c22d22c1-cf31-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&emdi=4a73c1c8-cf31-f111-9a48-000d3a14b640&ceid=954237)
